items.text: The systematic Nazi genocide of approximately six million Jews and millions of other victims, central to Nazi racial-ideological war aims.
The comprehensive mobilisation of industry, labour and civilian populations across the conflict’s global scope.
Prepare one turning-point timeline; for effects, use five headings — human cost, political map, superpowers, economy, decolonisation/international institutions.
Practise one analytical outline answering: “Explain the Second World War as both a military conflict and a racial-ideological war, and show how it created the post-1945 international order.”
Do not treat the Holocaust as a separate optional detail; it was central to Nazi racial war.
Do not explain Allied victory by one battle; industrial capacity, coalition warfare, geography and Axis strategic errors all mattered.
Do not say the atomic bombs alone caused Japan’s surrender without acknowledging the wider military situation and Soviet entry.
Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939; Britain and France declared war shortly afterward.
Germany invaded the Soviet Union in June 1941; Japan attacked Pearl Harbor in December 1941.
The Holocaust murdered about six million Jews and millions of other victims.
Germany surrendered in May 1945; Japan surrendered in August 1945 after the atomic bombings and Soviet entry into the war.
Present WWII as simultaneously a military conflict and an ideological-racial war, with the Holocaust integral to Nazi aims rather than a footnote.
The war’s effects (superpower rivalry, decolonisation, the UN, nuclear weapons) directly set up every subsequent topic in this subject.
